title: Wasteland
build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

records.c: Entry of the radio program: side 1, track 26, logical sector 17, 10 pages loaded to $7E00-$87FF by the game's Radio command ($8802: 'Radio (Y/N)?', then the game and the map saved at $880C, side 1 asked for at $880F, load_program at $881A). load_program ($03AD) reads the first sector to $5A00 and jumps through its word at +3, radio_load_address, which is $7E00: here. JMP radio_main.

The file header load_program reads from the first sector's copy at $5A03-$5A05: the load address $7E00, which is also where it starts the program (JMP ($5A03)), and the page count (radio_page_count). The radio itself never reads these three bytes.
$0A: the program is 10 pages, $7E00-$87FF; load_program takes the count from $5A05.

The fanfare, on SID voice 1, before the Cochise reward ($7EF0) and before each promotion ($7FC3): six notes with frequency values $2187, $2187, $2187, $2A3E, $2CC1, $323C (fanfare_notes_lo/hi), held 2, 1, 1, 2, 2 and 4 steps (fanfare_note_lengths). Each is started by sid_start_note (triangle, gate on), held by fanfare_hold, ended with $D404 = 0 and followed by delay_a with A = $30. By f = value x clock / 16777216 the notes are C5 C5 C5 E5 F5 G5 (523.2, 659.2, 698.4 and 783.9 Hz) at the NTSC clock, 1,022,727 Hz; at the PAL clock, 985,248 Hz, every one is 65 cents flat (504.0 to 755.2 Hz).
Low bytes of the six notes' SID frequency values, $87 $87 $87 $3E $C1 $3C, read at $7E08 into note_freq_lo.
High bytes of the six notes' frequency values, $21 $21 $21 $2A $2C $32, read at $7E0E into note_freq_hi: with fanfare_notes_lo, $2187 three times, then $2A3E, $2CC1 and $323C.
How long each of the six notes is held, in fanfare_hold rounds (X, read at $7E19): 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 4.
Holds a note: X rounds of delay_a ($04F0) with A = $C0, whose loop turns A x (A + 1) / 2 times, 18,528 for $C0. Returns X = 0.

Starts a note on SID voice 1 from the 11-byte record at $7E98 (X = 0): control $D404 = 0 first (gate off), then the frequency $D400/$D401 (note_freq_lo/hi), $D418 (fanfare_volume), the filter registers $D415-$D417 (all 0), pulse width $D402/$D403, attack/decay $D405 and sustain/release $D406, and last $D404 = $11 (fanfare_control), triangle with the gate on, which starts the sound.
$00, the value sid_start_note writes to $D405, attack/decay ($7E85).
$C0, the value sid_start_note writes to $D406, sustain/release ($7E8B).
$11, written to $D404 last ($7E91): waveform bit 4, triangle, with bit 0, the gate, on, which starts the note; play_fanfare writes 0 to end it ($7E21).
$8C, written to $D402, the pulse width's low byte ($7E79): width $058C with fanfare_pulse_hi.
$05, written to $D403, the pulse width's high byte ($7E7F).
$00, written to $D415, the first of the filter registers ($7E67).
$00, written to $D416, a filter register ($7E6D).
$00, written to $D417, a filter register ($7E73).
Frequency low byte for $D400, read at $7E55: play_fanfare stores each note's here first ($7E0B); 0 in the file.
Frequency high byte for $D401, read at $7E5B, stored at $7E11 for each note; 0 in the file.
$0F, written to $D418 ($7E61): master volume 15 in the low nibble, the high nibble 0.

The radio's main line. CLD and the stack pointer reset to $FF: the radio never returns, it ends by loading the game (return_to_game). Shows the roster again (roster_show, $02B7), copies 'Ranger Ctr.' (radio_caption) to the caption $F4D0 and shows portrait 8, a man holding a rifle (show_picture, $0419). Then the Cochise rewards ($7EBC), the promotions ($7F0B) and return_to_game ($8190). It does not look at where the party is: no map number or position is read, only the records and records_in_use $0A.

The reward for destroying Base Cochise, once for each character. For each record 1 to $0A (records_in_use, select_character): when it is conscious (is_conscious, $02C3), bit 0 of +$4B is set (module 4 sets it in every record in use when the base blows up, its $CA0B) and bit 0 of +$4C is clear, +$4C bit 0 is set so that it is given once; message 61, the Ranger Center's congratulations, is printed for the first such character of the call (cochise_text_shown); then portrait 11, a man in sunglasses and a shirt with two breast pockets, the fanfare, the text window (text_window_select, $0383) and distribute_points with 10 points (text_count $38 = 10): MAXCON +10 and 10 points for the attributes.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $7EDF: 0 in the file, raised at $7EE8 once message 61 has been printed, so the congratulations come once a radio call however many characters are rewarded.

Operand of the LDA #imm at $7F00: the record number, 1 to $0A, that cochise_rewards and promotions are on; stored at $7EBE and $7F0D before select_character, read at $7EFA and $7FF9 for distribute_points and at $8007 for the next record.

The promotions, after the rewards: for each record 1 to $0A (records_in_use), select_character and, when the character is conscious (is_conscious), promote_check. An unconscious character is passed over without a word ($7F18, next_promotion_record).

Is the character due a promotion? r = rank (+$24) + 1 goes to rank_plus_one. The threshold, 512 x r x r - 512 x r = 512 x r x (r - 1), is built in promotion_threshold: r added r times ($7F32), shifted left nine times ($7F4D), less r shifted left nine times in $1C-$1E ($7F5B-$7F87). Experience (+$21-$23, 24 bits) at or above it promotes ($7FBB); below it, or with a threshold that does not fit in 24 bits (r 182 and above, so nobody is promoted past rank 181), not_promoted. From rank k the next needs 1,024 x (1 + 2 + ... + k) experience: 1,024 at rank 1, 3,072 at rank 2, 6,144 at rank 3, 16,680,960 at rank 180.

Operand of the LDX #imm at $7F30: r, the rank being tested for, rank (+$24) + 1 (stored at $7F1F, raised at $7F22). It is the count and the addend of the multiplication ($7F32), the value shifted into $1C-$1E ($7F61), the index into rank_name_table ($7FC6) and, after a promotion, the new rank written to +$24 ($7FE9).

The end of each conscious character's turn: portrait 8 again, message 59 '<name> doesn't have quite enough experience to be considered for ', message 60 'another ' when the character has been promoted in this call (promoted_count), and message 62 'promotion.' with the (RETURN) prompt; then next_promotion_record. Seen in play-radio for Hell Razor, rank 1 with experience 0 (rank 2 needs 1,024).

Operand of the LDA #imm at $7FAA: how many promotions the current character has had in this call, raised at $7FBB and cleared at $8004 before the next record; non-zero adds 'another' to not_promoted's message.

A promotion to rank r: promoted_count up, portrait 11 and the fanfare, then message 56 '<name> has achieved the rank of ', or 57 '<name> is still a ' when rank_name_table gives rank r the same name as rank r - 1, and the name (rank_name_table[r]), which copy_rank_name also writes to +$32. Then +$24 = r, message 58 '. You get 2 adventure points to distribute among your stats.' and the (RETURN) prompt (text_count $38 = 2), distribute_points (MAXCON +2 and 2 points), and back to promote_check: one call can promote a character several times.
promoted_count back to 0 and on to the next record; after record $0A (records_in_use), return_to_game.
Low byte of the 24-bit promotion threshold (with $801A and $801B), cleared at $7F25 and built by promote_check: r x r, times 512, less 512 x r. Experience is compared with it at $7F8A. 0 in the file.
Middle byte of the promotion threshold (cleared at $7F2A; $7F3E, $7F50, $7F7A-$7F7F, $7F95).
High byte of the promotion threshold. A carry out of it, in the addition ($7F43-$7F46) or the nine doublings ($7F56), means a threshold past 24 bits, and no promotion.

Gives a character points to spend. A = the record (kept in record_in_menu), text_count $38 = the number of points (10 for the Cochise reward, 2 for a promotion). MAXCON (+$1B/+$1C) goes up by the number at once (add_to_maxcon, $8021, with no check against 32,767). Then, until the points are spent, the text window shows '<name> has N points to distribute.', 'Choose an attribute:' and eight rows, 1) Strength to 7) Charisma with the values at +$0E to +$14 and 8) Maxcon with +$1B/+$1C (show_points_menu, $8024-$8050), and each key 1-8 spends a point (choose_attribute), except a key it refuses, which keeps the point: an attribute already at 255, or key 8 when MAXCON + 1 reaches $8000.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $803B: the record offset of the attribute row being printed, $0E to $14 (set at $802E), stepped on until $15.

Waits for a key from attribute_keys, '1' to '8' (wait_listed_key, $02E4). The left-arrow key, which returns $FF, is ignored: all the points have to be spent. Key 8 adds 1 to MAXCON (add_to_maxcon); if that reaches $8000, MAXCON is set back to 32,767 ($7FFF) and the key refused, the point kept. Otherwise the character's roster line is redrawn when it is in the current party ($8079), since the roster shows MAX. Keys 1-7 go to raise_attribute.

Operand of the LDA #imm at $8079: the record whose points are being spent (stored by distribute_points at $801C). party_has_record ($02B4) looks for it in the current party and gives its position in Y to roster_line ($0297).

Keys 1-7: the attribute at +$0E plus the key's index (ST, IQ, LK, SP, AGL, DEX, CHR) goes up by 1. At 255 it stays and the key is refused, the point kept ($8096). IQ (+$0F) also raises SKP (+$20) by 1, unless SKP is 255, when the point is spent all the same.
One point spent (text_count $38 down by 1). With none left the window is cleared by a JMP to clear_window ($025C), whose RTS returns from distribute_points; otherwise the menu is drawn again ($8024).

Adds A to MAXCON (+$1B/+$1C, 16 bits) of the current character. Returns Y = $1C and A = the new high byte, N set from $8000 up. Called with the number of points ($8021, unchecked) and with 1 for key 8 ($8068, which checks N).
The keys the attribute menu takes, for wait_listed_key: '1' to '8' as $B1-$B8 (bit 7 set, as the keyboard routine returns them), then a zero. Index 0-6 is an attribute, 7 is MAXCON.

The menu's first string, printed by print_string_wrapped ($026F), which leaves $31/$32 after the zero, at the next: '{04}{0B} has {0F} point{0A}{0A}s{0A} to distribute.' (clear the window, the name, the count $38, 'point' or 'points'), two new lines, 'Choose an attribute:', a new line and '1) Strength  :', after which distribute_points prints the value ($8038).

The other rows, each a new line ($0D), its text and a zero: '2) IQ/Skill  :', '3) Luck      :', '4) Speed     :', '5) Agility   :', '6) Dexterity :', '7) Charisma  :' (each followed by the value at +$0F to +$14), '8) Maxcon    :' (followed by MAXCON, print_word $02F9), and at $8182 '{08}', which draws what is waiting in the word-wrap buffer.
'Ranger Ctr.' and a zero, the 12 bytes radio_main copies at $7EAC to picture_caption, $F4D0-$F4DB, the caption under the picture (seen under portrait 8 in play-radio).

Back to the game: picture animation off ($AC = 0), game_entry_step $92 = 0 (the game then starts without the step in place it takes after the start-up), side 1 awaited (check_side_1, $02D5) and the game program loaded from track 31, logical sector 9 (load_program, $03AD): 72 pages over $7E00-$C5FF, the radio included, started at $7E00. The radio writes nothing to disk; what it changed stays in the records at $F500-$FBFF, which that load leaves alone.

An entry nothing uses: STX $23 / STY $24 put the text cursor at column X, row Y, and it runs on into print_radio_message. No JSR or JMP $81A4 is anywhere in memory in either radio snapshot. The game's own print routine has the same four bytes at $7F4C, before its $7F50, and the game's snapshot holds no JSR or JMP $7F4C either.

Prints message A of the radio's text: word-wrapped output (output_wrapped, $0302), $43/$44 pointed at the radio's block (select_radio_text), print_message ($0311). The same code as the game's $7F50, with the radio's text address.
text_block $43/$44 = $82D9, the radio's packed text, for print_message and find_message.

Writes rank name A (a message number from rank_name_table) into the current record from +$32 on, decoded, with its zero: find_message ($0314), then text_char ($03DA) a character at a time. The longest name, 'Lieutenant Commander', fills +$32 to +$46.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $81CA: the record offset for the next character of the rank name, $32 up (set at $81C4, raised at $81D2).

Rank to name: 256 bytes, the message number (1-55) of the name of rank 0-255, read with the new rank at $7FC9 and with the one below it at $7FCE. Ranks 0 and 1 are Private (message 1); ranks 2-11 have a name each (Private 1st class to Master Grenadier); 12-29 share names in twos (Sergeant to Command Cadet), 30-74 in threes (2nd Lieutenant to Major Argent) and 75-130 in fours (Lance Colonel to Technical General). From 131 every rank is General Argent except 141 Imperial Scarscalp, 151 1st Class Fargo, 161 Photon Stud, 171 Revenant Argent and 181 Supreme Jerk. Past 181, which promote_check never passes, the five come round again, one every ten ranks from 191 to 231, and once more at 251-255.
$EA, between rank_name_table and the text. Nothing reads it: rank_name_table is read at most at $82D7 (index 255), and the text starts at $82D9.

The radio's packed text (select_radio_text): first the 60-byte alphabet the 5-bit codes index. Entries 0-38 are 'e anrotics', the end code $00 (entry 10), 'ldmughpfwyvbj."', $07, $0D, $06, 'k1,', $0B, $0A, "'xq2" and $0F; 39-59 are $7F, which no message uses. Code $1E capitalises the next letter, $1F adds $1E to the next code. Then radio_text_groups and 63 messages: 0 is empty, 1-55 are the rank names, 56-62 the radio's sentences.

The group table: 16 offsets, from $8315, to the groups of four messages ($8337, $8352, $837C, $83A5, $83CF, $83F4, $841B, $8446, $846A, $8496, $84C5, $84F1, $8524, $8553, $857D, $85F0). find_message reads message A's at $8315 + 2 x (A / 4) and decodes past the messages before it in the group.

A 17th word, $9AA3, in the table's room (the first group starts 34 bytes, 17 words, after $8315). $8315 + $9AA3 is $1DB8, in the engine, not this text; the radio asks for no message past 62, in group 15, so nothing reads it.

Text group 0: message 0, empty (only the end code, bits 0-4 of $8337); rank names 1 'Private' (from bit 5 of $8337), 2 'Private 1st class' (from bit 2 of $833D), 3 'Specialist' (from bit 6 of $8349); the group ends in bit 1 of $8351.

Text group 1: rank names 4 'Senior Specialist' (from $8352), 5 'Corporal' (from bit 4 of $835E), 6 'Lance Corporal' (from bit 6 of $8364), 7 'Command Corporal' (from bit 3 of $836F); the group ends in bit 1 of $837B.

Text group 2: rank names 8 'Grenadier' (from $837C), 9 'Fire Grenadier' (from bit 7 of $8382), 10 'Grenadier Major' (from bit 4 of $838D), 11 'Master Grenadier' (from bit 6 of $8398); the group ends in bit 4 of $83A4.

Text group 3: rank names 12 'Sergeant' (from $83A5), 13 'Technical Sergeant' (from bit 2 of $83AB), 14 'Sergeant Major' (from bit 3 of $83B8), 15 'Master Sergeant' (from $83C3); the group ends in bit 1 of $83CE.

Text group 4: rank names 16 'Sergeant Argent' (from $83CF), 17 'Cadet' (from bit 2 of $83DA), 18 'Cadet Specialist' (from bit 5 of $83DE), 19 'Combat Cadet' (from bit 4 of $83EA); the group ends in bit 6 of $83F3.

Text group 5: rank names 20 'Command Cadet' (from $83F4), 21 '2nd Lieutenant' (from $83FE), 22 '1st Lieutenant' (from bit 5 of $8408), 23 'Lieutenant' (from bit 2 of $8413); the group ends in bit 5 of $841A.

Text group 6: rank names 24 'Fireteam Lieutenant' (from $841B), 25 'Lieutenant Argent' (from bit 6 of $8428), 26 'Captain' (from bit 2 of $8435), 27 'Combat Captain' (from bit 7 of $843A); the group ends in bit 3 of $8445.

Text group 7: rank names 28 'Tech Captain' (from $8446), 29 'Command Captain' (from bit 3 of $844F), 30 'Captain Argent' (from bit 5 of $845A), 31 'Major' (from bit 2 of $8465); the group ends in bit 4 of $8469.

Text group 8: rank names 32 'Fireteam Major' (from $846A), 33 'Specialist Major' (from bit 5 of $8474), 34 'Technical Major' (from bit 4 of $8480), 35 'Major Argent' (from bit 6 of $848B); the group ends in bit 0 of $8495.

Text group 9: rank names 36 'Lance Colonel' (from $8496), 37 'Lieutenant Colonel' (from $84A0), 38 'Fireteam Colonel' (from bit 1 of $84AD), 39 'Division Colonel' (from $84B9); the group ends in bit 6 of $84C4.

Text group 10: rank names 40 'Colonel Argent' (from $84C5), 41 'Lance Commander' (from bit 5 of $84CF), 42 'Lieutenant Commander' (from bit 7 of $84DA), 43 'Commander' (from bit 2 of $84E9); the group ends in bit 0 of $84F0.

Text group 11: rank names 44 'Technical Commander' (from $84F1), 45 'Force Commander' (from bit 6 of $84FE), 46 'Brigadier General' (from $850A), 47 'Lieutenant General' (from bit 4 of $8516); the group ends in bit 4 of $8523.

Text group 12: rank names 48 'Major General' (from $8524), 49 'Technical General' (from $852E), 50 'General Argent' (from bit 4 of $853A), 51 'Imperial Scarscalp' (from bit 1 of $8545); the group ends in bit 1 of $8552.

Text group 13: rank names 52 '1st Class Fargo' (from $8553), 53 'Photon Stud' (from bit 7 of $855E), 54 'Revenant Argent' (from bit 5 of $8567), 55 'Supreme Jerk' (from bit 7 of $8572); the group ends in bit 1 of $857C.

Text group 14, messages 56-59, the promotion sentences: 56 '{07}{0B} has achieved the rank of ' (open the text window, the name; $7FD5), 57 '{07}{0B} is still a ' (from bit 6 of $858F; $7FDD), 58 '. You get {0F} adventure point{0A}{0A}s{0A} to distribute among your stats.' with a new line and the (RETURN) prompt (from bit 6 of $8599; $7FF6), 59 '{07}{0B} doesn't have quite enough experience to be considered for ' (from bit 1 of $85C6 to bit 2 of $85EF; $7FA7).
Text group 15, messages 60-62: 60 'another ' (to bit 4 of $85F5; $7FB0), then 61 (cochise_congratulations) and 62 (msg_62_promotion). There is no message 63: what decodes after 62 is radio_file_tail.

Message 61, from bit 5 of $85F5 to bit 6 of $8740, printed by cochise_rewards ($7EE3): four screens, each opened with a fresh text window ({07}) and closed by (RETURN): '"Congratulations Rangers on a mission well done."' / '"Since you embarked on your mission we had reports from other rangers about the horrible strength contained in Base Cochise."' / '"Had it been possible, we would have warned you. However, we were afraid any such communication would have drawn Cochise's forces to you and would have destroyed your mission before you had a fair chance of succeeding."' / '"Even now, news of your victory is spreading through the Wasteland and your heroic efforts will be rewarded."', and a last {07}.

Message 62, from bit 7 of $8740 to the end of $8748: 'promotion.', a new line and the (RETURN) prompt ($7FB5). Its end code fills bits 3-7 of $8748, the last bits of the text; the decoder (text_bits, $291D) fetches a byte only when it needs a bit, so it never reads $8749.

$8749-$87FF, the end of the file, is nothing the radio uses: no operand of its code names an address past $82D7 other than the text pointer $82D9, and its last message ends in $8748. From $874B it is the game's own $874B-$87FF (the game file, T31/L9) byte for byte, except $87B4 ($71 here, $75 in the game) and $87B9 ($E2, game $E6), the operands of the game's JSR $BB75 and LDY $BAE6,X, each 4 lower; $8749-$874A ($A0 $20) differ from the game's $03 $4C. Probably whatever was in memory when the file was written (a guess).
